what_this_layer_is: The shape of what the DATABASE holds and mutates after import. Nothing here ships in a unit file. The distinction matters and was never stated: a unit file is tagged and immutable, so anything that changes after extraction — a student's query, a revision, a usage record — cannot live in it without breaking the tagging discipline the whole pipeline rests on.

companion_documents.procedure: extraction_procedure_v2 — how to read a source, and how it is verified

import_rule: The importer seeds the runtime record from a tagged unit file and never writes back to it. On import it recomputes content_hash under the current normalisation and KEEPS THE TAGGED HASH BESIDE IT (D18: Classes 6-9 migrate at import, not by re-issue). After import the database is authoritative; the file is provenance. PENDING CATEGORIES: a file's pending_category records where the question stood at extraction and never changes. At import the question's category is taken from the defect register's live row (viyamo-record/defects/instances), which is where triage moves, founds and closes instances. The file is never rewritten to follow a move.

Query.note: A user says an answer is wrong. This is the mechanism by which a better-informed student corrects a reviewer, which is the reason it exists.
Query.question_id: string — keys to the file layer
Query.claim: string — MANDATORY free text. A bare thumbs-down generates noise; a sentence generates signal

rca.cause_category: optional — the defect register category id, which is how one student's catch becomes a systemic fix
rca.swept: boolean — was the same shape searched for elsewhere
rca.swept_scope: 'question'|'unit'|'class'|'all' — which of the three levels was done
rca.swept_found: number — how many others carried it

QueryRules.never_overwrite: An upheld query produces a NEW revision in the RUNTIME record, keyed by question_id with revision as the join. The tagged file is immutable and is never written back to: its status_history holds the EXTRACTION-time trail only and stops there. Every later transition — review, an upheld query, retirement — is appended runtime-side. The trail therefore spans both layers by design, and this is the join: file = where it started, database = where it continues. Without stating that, the revision trail reads as if it lived in a frozen file.
QueryRules.mcq_identity: RULED 2026-09-21. content_hash (text only) is NOT a duplicate test for mcq/mcq_multi: two MCQs with the same stem and different option sets are SIBLINGS — both usable, never both in one paper (the generator excludes a sibling of a picked question). A DUPLICATE needs the same stem AND the same normalised option set AND the same key; only one of a duplicate pair is served. Case of record: sci-7-05-s1-q003/q018 are siblings (their `duplicate of` flag is wrong, corrected at review); sci-7-11-s1-q019/q021 are duplicates.
QueryRules.identity_survives: content_hash is computed over `text` only, so correcting an answer does not change the question's identity and its usage history stays attached. This is what makes blast radius answerable.
QueryRules.resolution_authority: approval_rules below. A student cannot resolve their own query. Student-audience content needs subject_teacher and management.
QueryRules.propagation_is_mandatory: `swept` and `swept_scope` must be filled before a query closes. Nobody may close one without answering 'did this happen elsewhere'. Three levels: fix this question; sweep the unit for the same shape; sweep every unit, because the cause is usually systemic — a parser rule or a source convention.
QueryRules.blast_radius: Usage names every paper that carried the wrong answer and every teacher who set it. For a marks-affecting error, notify those teachers; otherwise a silent fix is enough.
QueryRules.generator_hold: A question with an open answer-scope query is NOT drawn by the generator until it resolves.
QueryRules.feeds_the_register: An upheld query files an instance against its cause_category. A recurring complaint can therefore cross the register's threshold and become an amendment on its own.
QueryRules.the_metric: Queries per thousand questions served, split by rca.origin. If extraction_defect dominates, the gate needs work. If source_defect dominates, that is DSERT's problem and it is evidence to take upward rather than absorb.

BankTier.note: Most wrong answers are already known. Classes 6-9 carry 110 review-blocking flags today. Serving those and waiting for a student to catch them is strictly worse than not serving them. Tiering is the cheapest intervention available and does not need the query system at all.
BankTier.A: clean and reviewed OR machine-verified (rev 5) — the generator draws freely. A machine-verified question is marked as such on every answer key the generator renders
BankTier.B: flagged, category-pending, or authoring verdict 'cannot tell' — held back. Visible to the reviewer, never on a paper
BankTier.C: retired — kept for provenance, never served
BankTier.computed_from: source_flags, pending_category, authoring verification verdict, status, and open answer-scope queries; review state (ReviewState, rev 5)

ReviewState.note: RULED 2026-09-21 (Yash; review method v1.2), made a GENERAL RULE 2026-09-22 (all subjects, all classes): question banks go live without human review. The label must say so, everywhere a key is shown.
ReviewState.state: 'machine_verified'|'reviewed' — machine_verified = passed two independent AI science reads, or adjudicated with a reference and (for a changed key) checked by the coordinator. NEVER displayed or counted as 'reviewed'
ReviewState.outcome: 'kept'|'corrected'|'held'|'incomplete' — incomplete: key stays, marked for the authoring pass; held: tier B, never on a paper, and `state` does not apply
ReviewState.reference: optional {kind:'textbook'|'computation', book?, chapter?, printed_page?, quote?, working?} — REQUIRED when outcome is corrected
ReviewState.source: viyamo-record/review/class-N/review_state.json (one ReviewState per question of the tagged bank; written by review_apply.py, stage 4) — imported runtime-side like every later transition (QueryRules.never_overwrite)
ReviewState.correction: optional {answer: string, option_id: string|null} — present only when outcome is corrected: the new key text and, for an MCQ, the new option; the printed key stays in answer_as_printed; answer_provenance becomes 'ai'
ReviewState.route: 'kept'|'incomplete'|'stage3'|'stage4'|'hold_no_key'|'extra' — the merge route (review method v1.4) the outcome was decided under; audit only
ReviewState.reason: optional string — why held/incomplete/corrected, from the read or the verifier; audit and the decisions page

QueryIntake.note: RULED 2026-09-21 (Yash). Teachers report a wrong key by commenting ON THE QUESTION where it is displayed — no separate form. This ships with the FIRST release that displays questions; a display without it is incomplete. Each comment becomes a Query (raised_by.role='teacher'; claim = the comment text, mandatory).

MarkResult.criteria_results: optional [{criterion_id, marks_awarded}] — for a rubric answer

KeywordMatching.normalization: lowercase, strip punctuation, collapse spaces, light stemming (Latin only)
KeywordMatching.edit_distance_tolerance: <=4 chars exact; 5-8 one edit; 9+ two edits (Latin only)
KeywordMatching.verdicts: green correct; orange concept right / misspelled (half marks, spelling event logged); red wrong
KeywordMatching.UNSPECIFIED: Devanagari and Kannada normalisation is not specified and must be before any language pilot. The same gap exists in content_hash and is more dangerous there, because it silently breaks duplicate detection rather than visibly breaking marking.

query_resolution.note: the raiser may not resolve their own query

enforcement_note: Approval rules, status transitions, tiering and the send rule are enforced at app level. The schema carries truth; the app carries the lock.
revisions: 2026-09-21 rev 2 — the revision bridge to the file layer stated; the prior wording implied the post-import trail lived in the tagged file, which is immutable.
2026-09-21 rev 2 — companion reference corrected: it named extraction_procedure_v1, superseded by v2 the same day.
2026-09-21 rev 3 — import takes pending categories from the defect register, not the file; without this a triaged question could never leave the category it was extracted into.

2026-09-21 rev 4 — import IGNORES top-level unit keys the file schema does not define (Class 7 carries validated_checklist_result, report_summary, review_blocking_flags, state_notes, file_check). They stay in the tagged file as history and are never read as data. Import also treats all three forms of a drawn key as one fact: flag `answer is a diagram — no key text` + empty answer, the placeholder `[diagram answer — see page image]`, and junk values filed in the register (port mapping §6g).

2026-09-21 rev 5 — ReviewState (machine_verified vs reviewed; outcomes; references) and QueryIntake (comment on the displayed question, from the first release). BankTier A admits machine-verified questions, and every rendered answer key marks them. Generator requirement: the answer-key renderer shows the machine-verified mark per question.
2026-09-22 rev 5a — ReviewState: the no-human-review rule is general (all subjects), not Science 6-9 only (Yash).

2026-09-23 rev 6 — ReviewState: `correction`, `route`, `reason` fields and the source file review_state.json (stage 4, review_apply.py). A stem-only STEM_OK verdict leaves the key to the reads; every stage-4 item the verifier did not adjudicate is held.
